issues.note: Run A's per-document latency column sums to 496.7 s, but the report's run-level sum is 503.4 s (the serving export agrees: latency_sum_seconds 503.369, p50 26.595 s vs a per-row median of 26.0 s). The report says its per-document rows were reconstructed from captured stdout; scores in the same table do match the stated mean. Latency dots for Run A come from that table.

The SAND-032 program summary lists the MAUD-prompt merger run at $0.005461/doc; its run report gives $0.004275/doc. The summary row used the serving export, which also bills the run's 122.8 s cold boot (0.251214 vs 0.196653 USD over 46 docs); every other row is busy-window only. This page uses the busy-window figure.
eval-environment files the merger leg under Qwen3-8B, but the logged model is qwen/qwen3.7-flash. It is shown here as its own model.
The DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash n=100 classification run logs a 4.8 s wall time but a 32.0 s p95 call latency, which cannot both be true. Its runtime is not charted.

mailroom-ml Arm B eval JSON: selective_risk.coverage is 0.3771, which is the last sweep row (threshold 0.99, coverage 0.3771), not the recommended 0.9 threshold (0.8688). The page reads the recommended row.
mailroom-ml run-3 eval JSON has the same exporter defect: coverage 0.4325 is the 0.99 row; at the recommended 0.93 threshold coverage is 0.7321.

The held-out-plus eval (1,323 docs, doc_type accuracy 0.0128) is invalid: on the 323 canonical test documents it contains, it gets 17 right where the same checkpoint's canonical run gets 307. Its slice table also assigns all docs to the canonical slice. It is excluded from the charts.
